lesson.title: Code Duplication
lesson.summary: Understand code duplication from first principles, with a small runnable example.

stage.name: Object Tools & Design
stage.subtitle: Book chapters 5–6
stage.description: Namespaces, attributes, closures, generators, reflection, plus OOP design principles such as SOLID.

payload.markdown: Duplication is one of the great evils in code. If you get a strange sense of déjà vu as you write a routine, chances are you have a problem.

blocks.text: Duplication is one of the great evils in code. If you get a strange sense of déjà vu as you write a routine, chances are you have a problem.

payload.markdown: Take a look at the instances of repetition in your system. Perhaps they belong together. Duplication generally means tight coupling. If you change something fundamental about one routine, will the similar routines need amendment? If this is the case, they probably belong in the same class.

items: Classes & Objects: A class defines state and behaviour; objects are instances of that definition.
Coupling: How much one class leans on another's internals; good design keeps it low.
Abstract Classes: A partial base class that forces subclasses to complete certain methods.
UML Class & Sequence: Standard diagrams for static structure and runtime interaction.
Unit of Work: Tracking changes to many objects and writing them in a single transaction.
